How I help businesses automate the busy work
A short intro to how I help teams use AI automations to save time, find revenue leaks, and turn messy workflows into systems that compound.
Three collaborators working through an automation workflow together in a gritty music studio.

AI automation is most useful when it is tied to a real business outcome: faster follow-up, cleaner operations, better content production, stronger customer experiences, or more time for the work that actually moves revenue.

That is where I like to help.

My background sits across full-stack development, AI tooling, content strategy, growth marketing, and product work. I have built courses and labs that teach people how generative AI works, created internal AI tools for content teams, and now work as an AI Product Engineer at [Gametime](https://gametime.co), where I build AI tools and product systems for live event discovery.

The common thread is simple: take a messy, manual, ambiguous process and turn it into something useful.

## Where automation can make money

Most teams do not need a giant AI transformation project. They need a few specific workflows that remove friction from the business.

That might mean automating lead research so sales teams spend less time gathering context and more time starting good conversations. It might mean turning scattered customer notes into usable insights for product and marketing. It might mean building a content pipeline that helps a small team publish more consistently without lowering the quality bar.

Good automation does not replace judgment. It gives better leverage to the people who already have it.

## How I can help

I can help you identify the workflows worth automating, prototype the first version, and turn the useful pieces into repeatable systems.

That can look like:

- AI-assisted sales and lead research workflows
- Internal tools that reduce repetitive content or operations work
- Marketing and content pipelines that help small teams move faster
- Product workflows that use AI to improve customer experience
- Data cleanup, enrichment, and reporting automations
- Lightweight prototypes that prove whether an AI idea is worth building

The best projects usually start with a simple question: where are smart people on your team still doing work that a system could prepare, organize, summarize, route, or draft for them?

## What I care about

I care about automations that are practical, measurable, and easy for real teams to use. The point is not to bolt AI onto a workflow because it sounds interesting. The point is to make the business run better.

If an automation saves hours, improves response time, helps a team ship more, or uncovers revenue that was being missed, it is doing its job.

That is the kind of work I want to build more of.

Back To The Start Band Website
A high-energy band website that turns the feeling of a live Coldplay tribute show into a clear path for fans, venues, and booking partners.
Back To The Start website hero featuring the band performing beneath golden stage lights and a prominent Coldplay tribute wordmark.

## Overview

[Back To The Start](https://backtothestart.band/) is a Coldplay tribute band built around an uplifting, full-scale live experience. I designed and developed the complete website to carry that energy beyond the stage and give fans, venues, and booking partners a focused place to experience the band.

The site brings the band's story, live footage, tour dates, electronic press kit, audience signup, and booking contact into one visual system. It feels like the show while still making the next step obvious for every visitor.

## The Challenge

A band website has to serve several audiences at once. Fans want dates, music, and a sense of the live experience. Talent buyers need a quick way to assess the act, review production information, and start a booking conversation. The band needs a home it can keep using as shows, media, and momentum grow.

The design had to create atmosphere without burying those practical jobs. Every section needed to feel expressive, load clearly, and move visitors toward seeing, following, or booking the band.

## The Experience

### The live show leads the story

Full-bleed performance photography, bold typography, saturated color, and motion-inspired details establish the mood immediately. The visual language draws from concert posters and stage lighting while keeping the page legible and direct.

### Different visitors get clear paths

The homepage introduces the show and routes fans toward live dates and video. Booking calls to action stay visible, and the dedicated electronic press kit gives venue teams the band bio, live footage, promotional assets, production documents, and contact details in one place.

### Real tools sit inside the brand

The site integrates live tour listings, an embedded performance reel, and email signup without making them feel like disconnected widgets. Each functional element is framed as part of the same experience.

### The system works across screens

Responsive layouts preserve the scale and rhythm of the art direction on mobile, where fans are most likely to arrive from social posts or a venue listing. Navigation, media, and calls to action remain easy to use without flattening the personality of the site.

## What I Built

- A custom responsive homepage and visual design system
- Band positioning, show storytelling, and member presentation
- Live tour-date integration and fan calls to action
- A complete electronic press kit for talent buyers and venues
- Embedded live video, promotional imagery, and downloadable production resources
- Email-list signup, social discovery, and direct booking paths
- Search and social metadata for a polished shared-link experience

## My Role

Product strategy, information architecture, UX and visual design, responsive frontend development, content structure, third-party integrations, SEO foundations, and launch.

## Why It Matters

The strongest music sites do more than hold information. They translate a feeling into action. Back To The Start now has a digital home that presents the scale of the show, helps fans find the next date, and gives booking partners what they need to move from interest to inquiry.

A high-impact transportation website that makes a diverse Raleigh fleet easy to compare and turns group plans into a direct path to rates, quotes, and booking.
Capital City Transportation homepage featuring a party bus at night and the headline Raleigh Party Bus and Limo Rentals.

## Overview

[Capital City Transportation](https://rdubusrental.netlify.app/) provides party buses, Sprinter limos, and executive shuttles for groups across Raleigh, Durham, Chapel Hill, and the Triangle. I designed and built a complete website that turns a broad fleet and wide range of occasions into a clear, energetic booking experience.

The site combines vehicle discovery, passenger capacity, package information, service use cases, local expertise, and direct support in one cohesive system. It gives customers enough detail to compare their options while keeping the excitement of the event—not the logistics—at the center of the story.

## The Challenge

Group transportation customers arrive with different plans, budgets, headcounts, and expectations. A wedding coordinator may prioritize timing and comfort, while a birthday group wants atmosphere and a corporate team needs professional service. The website had to make those choices understandable without turning the experience into a dense vehicle catalog.

It also needed to compete for high-intent local searches, establish trust quickly, and create a useful path from browsing to booking for both decisive customers and people who still need help choosing.

## The Experience

### Make the arrival feel like the product

The opening pairs a dramatic nighttime vehicle image with oversized typography and the line “Arrive like you mean it.” The site immediately positions transportation as part of the occasion rather than a utility that happens before it.

### Organize the fleet around real decisions

Party buses, Sprinter limos, and executive shuttles are presented with distinct personalities, passenger ranges, photography, and direct routes to deeper fleet pages. Customers can quickly move from group size and desired atmosphere to the right category.

### Serve celebrations and practical trips

Weddings, birthdays, bachelor and bachelorette parties, game days, corporate outings, airport transfers, and nights out each receive a clear place in the experience. The structure helps visitors recognize their plan while showing the range of the business.

### Offer two paths to conversion

Customers ready to commit can view rates and book online. Those with a more complex itinerary can share their date, party size, occasion, and stops through a focused quote flow or call the team directly.

### Build a local search foundation

Dedicated fleet and service architecture, Raleigh and Triangle copy, semantic page structure, local business data, and social metadata give the company a strong base for commercial search visibility without compromising the brand experience.

## What I Built

- A custom responsive multipage website and visual design system
- Positioning and conversion copy for a premium group-transportation brand
- Fleet architecture for party buses, Sprinter limos, and executive shuttles
- Service paths for weddings, celebrations, corporate events, airport trips, and game days
- Passenger-capacity and package guidance to support vehicle selection
- Online booking, custom quote, text, and direct phone conversion paths
- Accessible mobile navigation and responsive vehicle presentation
- Local SEO, structured business data, canonical, and social sharing foundations

## My Role

Product strategy, positioning, information architecture, UX and visual design, conversion copy, responsive frontend development, content structure, accessibility, local SEO foundations, booking architecture, and launch.

## Why It Matters

A transportation website has to make logistics feel simple without making the service feel generic. Capital City now has a digital presence that captures the energy of its fleet, helps each customer find the right ride, and turns a complicated group plan into a clear next step.

Elevated Photo Booths homepage featuring a joyful group photo and the headline The party looks good on you.

## Overview

[Elevated Photo Booths](https://elevatedphotobooths.netlify.app/) provides premium photo booth rentals for weddings, corporate events, parties, proms, and quinceañeras across Raleigh–Durham and beyond. I designed and built a complete website that presents the company as an experience partner—not simply an equipment rental.

The site brings four booth options, the event experience, social proof, the veteran-owned business story, and a focused quote flow into one expressive system. It gives prospective clients the confidence to choose a booth while keeping the energy and spontaneity of a great celebration front and center.

## The Challenge

Photo booth businesses often rely on similar lists of features, which makes it difficult for a customer to understand why one experience will feel different from another. Elevated needed a site that could communicate both the quality of the output and the warmth of the service behind it.

The website also had to make four distinct offerings easy to compare, work for several event types, and move visitors from inspiration to a useful inquiry without flattening the personality of the brand.

## The Experience

### Let the guests sell the feeling

The opening uses a full-screen celebration photograph, editorial typography, and the line “The party looks good on you.” The first impression is built around the outcome clients want: their favorite people relaxed, connected, and having a genuinely good time.

### Make every booth easy to understand

The DSLR Studio Booth, 360 Video Booth, iPad Selfie Booth, and All-Day Drop-Off each get a clear visual card, concise description, and best-fit event cues. Visitors can scan the lineup quickly or select a booth to carry that choice directly into the quote form.

### Turn service into part of the product

The three-step experience explains how the team helps choose, customize, deliver, support, and collect each setup. Reviews and the veteran-owned story reinforce that the value is not only in the camera—it is in having the event handled well.

### Keep the inquiry personal

The quote flow asks for the date, event type, booth preference, and a little about the vision. It gives the team useful context for a helpful response while keeping the interaction light and low-pressure for the customer.

### Carry the energy across screens

Responsive layouts preserve the oversized type, immersive imagery, booth comparisons, and clear calls to action on mobile. Navigation and forms remain straightforward even as the art direction stays bold.

## What I Built

- A custom responsive website and event-focused visual design system
- Brand positioning and conversion copy centered on the guest experience
- Clear presentation and comparison of four photo booth offerings
- A guided three-step explanation of planning and event-day service
- Review, trust, service-area, and veteran-owned business storytelling
- A booth-aware quote experience with direct phone and email paths
- Accessible navigation, semantic content, and mobile interaction patterns
- Local search, structured business data, and social sharing foundations

Garden & Art Landscapes homepage featuring a lush garden path and the headline Landscapes with a point of view.

## Overview

[Garden & Art Landscapes](https://www.landscapingraleigh.com/) is a Raleigh landscape design, installation, and garden-care company founded by horticulturist and artist Norman Rabins. I designed and built the complete website to give the business a digital presence as distinctive as the landscapes it creates.

The site brings together finished work, practical services, Norman's experience, original garden art, and a direct inquiry path. It presents the company as more than a landscaping contractor: a practice shaped by horticultural knowledge and an artist's eye.

## The Opportunity

Garden & Art already had the strongest raw materials for a compelling website: more than 20 years of local experience, deep plant knowledge, a broad range of built work, and an unusual creative point of view. The challenge was turning those strengths into a clear story that homeowners could understand quickly.

The website needed to feel elevated without becoming precious. It also had to explain a wide service offering, establish local credibility, show the quality of the work, and make it easy for a homeowner to start a conversation.

## The Experience

### Lead with a point of view

The opening pairs immersive garden photography with editorial typography and the line "Landscapes with a point of view." The art direction immediately distinguishes the company while concise supporting copy explains what it does and where it works.

### Let completed work build trust

A visual portfolio shows retaining walls, ponds, gates, paths, patios, fireplaces, planting beds, and other finished landscapes. The imagery gives prospective clients tangible proof and helps them imagine the range of projects the company can take on.

### Make a broad offering understandable

Eight services—from landscape design and hardscapes to water systems, lighting, garden care, sod, seasonal cleanups, and tree work—are organized into a consistent, scannable system. Visitors can understand the whole practice without navigating a maze of pages.

### Put expertise behind the work

Norman's story connects his horticultural training, experience at the New York Botanical Garden, teaching, certifications, and artistic practice to the way he approaches a site. A dedicated gallery of original metalwork makes the creative dimension of the business visible rather than merely claiming it.

### Turn interest into a useful inquiry

Calls to action lead into a concise project form that asks for the information needed to begin a real conversation. Phone, email, location, license, and service-area details reinforce trust without interrupting the visual experience.

## The Growth Foundation

The website also serves as the foundation for a broader local marketing system. Service architecture, search metadata, real project imagery, and owner expertise can support search-led pages and useful content over time. The accompanying 90-day plan connects that foundation to ongoing publishing, campaign reuse, and inquiry measurement.

The site comes first: a credible destination that future search, social, email, and local campaigns can confidently send people to.

## What I Built

- A custom responsive website and visual design system
- Positioning and content architecture around the company's point of view
- A project portfolio built from real landscape photography
- Clear presentation of eight core service areas
- Founder, experience, certification, and original-art storytelling
- A focused project-inquiry experience with direct contact options
- Accessibility, local SEO, structured metadata, and social sharing foundations
- A content and measurement roadmap for continued growth

## My Role

Product strategy, information architecture, UX and visual design, responsive frontend development, content structure, local SEO foundations, inquiry flow, growth planning, and launch.

## Why It Matters

The new site makes the business easier to understand without sanding away what makes it unusual. Garden & Art now has a digital home that shows the quality of its work, explains the expertise behind it, and gives local homeowners a clear reason—and a clear way—to get in touch.

## Overview

[Oak City Shuttle](https://oakcityshuttle.netlify.app/) provides private party bus and group transportation for weddings, brewery tours, birthdays, game days, corporate events, and nights out across Raleigh and the Triangle. I designed and built a complete website that makes the ride feel like part of the memory while keeping the planning experience straightforward.

The site combines event-focused services, bus amenities, a simple booking process, customer reviews, practical FAQs, and a fast quote flow in one high-energy visual system. It gives groups a compelling reason to ride together and an easy way to start organizing the details.

## The Challenge

The core value of a private shuttle is emotional and practical at the same time. The whole group stays together, the celebration starts earlier, and no one has to solve parking, rideshares, or designated-driver logistics. The website needed to communicate all of that instantly.

Oak City also serves several different occasions with a focused fleet. The site had to show the versatility of the service, answer common planning questions, and turn interest into a quote without presenting the business like a generic directory of vehicles.

## The Experience

### Start with the people, not the bus

The hero leads with a real group gathered beside the shuttle and the line “Your ride should be part of the story.” Bold condensed type, a route-ticket graphic, and celebration photography make the experience feel social, local, and full of momentum.

### Give each occasion a clear use case

Weddings, brewery tours, birthdays, nights out, corporate events, and game days are explained through the problem each customer is trying to solve. Every service leads naturally toward planning that specific ride.

### Make one bus feel versatile

Interior photography and a focused amenity list show how lounge seating, Bluetooth audio, built-in coolers, lighting, and air conditioning turn the bus into a private space for up to 30 people. The story stays centered on what those features enable for the group.

### Reduce the plan to three steps

The route-inspired booking section moves from sharing the plan, to confirming the itinerary and quote, to bringing the crew. Reviews and FAQs handle the common trust and logistics questions alongside that simple process.

### Keep conversion close on every screen

Calls to phone, text, and request a quote remain easy to reach throughout the page. The form captures the occasion, date, group size, pickup, and stops while mobile actions stay fixed and direct.

## What I Built

Overview

Oak City Shuttle provides private party bus and group transportation for weddings, brewery tours, birthdays, game days, corporate events, and nights out across Raleigh and the Triangle. I designed and built a complete website that makes the ride feel like part of the memory while keeping the planning experience straightforward.

The site combines event-focused services, bus amenities, a simple booking process, customer reviews, practical FAQs, and a fast quote flow in one high-energy visual system. It gives groups a compelling reason to ride together and an easy way to start organizing the details.

The Challenge

The core value of a private shuttle is emotional and practical at the same time. The whole group stays together, the celebration starts earlier, and no one has to solve parking, rideshares, or designated-driver logistics. The website needed to communicate all of that instantly.

Oak City also serves several different occasions with a focused fleet. The site had to show the versatility of the service, answer common planning questions, and turn interest into a quote without presenting the business like a generic directory of vehicles.

The Experience

Start with the people, not the bus

The hero leads with a real group gathered beside the shuttle and the line “Your ride should be part of the story.” Bold condensed type, a route-ticket graphic, and celebration photography make the experience feel social, local, and full of momentum.

Give each occasion a clear use case

Weddings, brewery tours, birthdays, nights out, corporate events, and game days are explained through the problem each customer is trying to solve. Every service leads naturally toward planning that specific ride.

Make one bus feel versatile

Interior photography and a focused amenity list show how lounge seating, Bluetooth audio, built-in coolers, lighting, and air conditioning turn the bus into a private space for up to 30 people. The story stays centered on what those features enable for the group.

Reduce the plan to three steps

The route-inspired booking section moves from sharing the plan, to confirming the itinerary and quote, to bringing the crew. Reviews and FAQs handle the common trust and logistics questions alongside that simple process.

Keep conversion close on every screen

Calls to phone, text, and request a quote remain easy to reach throughout the page. The form captures the occasion, date, group size, pickup, and stops while mobile actions stay fixed and direct.

## Overview

[ZimZoom Photo Booth](https://zimzoom.netlify.app/) creates photo booth experiences for weddings, parties, university events, and brand activations across North Carolina. I designed and built a complete website that captures the energy of the events while giving customers a clear way to compare experiences, see the work, and check their date.

The site brings six services, real event photography, customization options, statewide locations, reviews, FAQs, and booking into one bold visual system. It presents ZimZoom as more than a booth rental: an experienced creative partner that knows how to make a room come alive.

## The Challenge

ZimZoom has substantial proof—thousands of events, millions of photos, recognizable clients, strong reviews, and a broad service area. The challenge was organizing all of that credibility without losing the playful personality that makes the brand memorable.

The website also needed to distinguish six related experiences, work for both private celebrations and brand events, and give visitors enough information to choose confidently without slowing down the path to availability.

## The Experience

### Open with unmistakable energy

The hero combines real guest photography, oversized typography, animated details, and the promise of “Extraordinary Photo Booth Experiences.” The first screen establishes the brand as colorful, social, and polished while keeping the primary action—checking a date—immediately visible.

### Turn six services into six personalities

Pro, Glam, 360, LITE, Headshots, and Event Photo each receive a distinct card, visual treatment, and plain-language explanation. The system helps visitors understand the difference between experiences while showing that they all belong to the same brand.

### Let scale and real work build trust

Event totals, photo counts, client logos, gallery images, reviews, and media recognition work together as layered proof. Wedding guests, corporate teams, university groups, and event planners can all find evidence that feels relevant to their occasion.

### Make customization tangible

Backdrops, graphics, branded interfaces, galleries, and sharing experiences are presented as visible parts of the product. The site shows customers how ZimZoom can feel specific to their wedding, organization, or campaign instead of relying on a generic customization claim.

### Connect statewide reach to conversion

Dedicated location presentation establishes service across Raleigh, Durham, Charlotte, Asheville, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, and Wilmington. The final booking flow carries the event details into ZimZoom's live request system while phone and gallery paths remain close at hand.

## What I Built

- A custom responsive website and high-energy visual design system
- Brand positioning and conversion copy for private and corporate events
- Clear presentation of six distinct photo and event experiences
- A gallery system built around real event imagery and customization examples
- Client, event-volume, review, and media-recognition proof sections
- Statewide location and service-area storytelling
- A guided availability form connected to the live booking workflow
- Accessible navigation, responsive interactions, and mobile conversion paths

## My Role

Product strategy, positioning, information architecture, UX and visual design, conversion copy, responsive frontend development, content structure, accessibility, booking flow, and launch.

## Why It Matters

ZimZoom already knew how to make events memorable. The new site gives that experience a digital expression with the same confidence and personality. Visitors can now feel the energy, understand the options, trust the team behind them, and move naturally from inspiration to availability.
